part.text:
Fixed in `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleBuilderDefault.java:74`.

**Root cause:** When `@Builder.Default` moves a field's initializing expression into the generated `$default$foo()` method, `recursiveSetGeneratedBy` (via `setGeneratedBy`, JavacHandlerUtil.java:177) stamps the `@Builder` annotation's position onto *every* node of the moved user code. javac resolves/caches method-invocation types by position (see the same quirk documented at HandleBuilder.java:655 for `@ObtainVia`), so multiple invocations in the initializer that all end up with the same position get their types mixed up — `myChar()` was resolved with `myInt()`'s type, producing `MyClass<Integer> cannot be converted to MyClass<Character>` / `inference variable T has incompatible bounds`. Java 8 was unaffected because its javac didn't cache this way.

**Fix:** `generateDefaultProvider` now records the original start and end positions of the user's initializer subtree before the generated-by marking, and restores them afterward, so the moved expression keeps its distinct, parser-accurate positions.
